function.name: mdp_search_blocks
function.description: PRIMARY ENTRY POINT when the user's question contains identifiable keywords (topics, technical terms, named entities, numbers). Call this FIRST before mdp_list_blocks — keyword search reaches candidate blocks more efficiently than scanning the full manifest. Case-insensitive substring match across each block's title, summary, id, type, tags, status, keywords (author-declared ∪ auto-extracted N-gram/PMI keyword list), and body markdown. Snippets are always truncated context windows, never full body — so scanning body costs nothing on the response side. Use `limit` to cap result count. Two call modes: single keyword via `query`, or multi-keyword OR via `any_of` (preferred — fan out several candidate terms in ONE call instead of N round-trips). Returns [{id, type, status, title, line, keywords, matched, snippets}] where `matched` lists which input keywords hit and `snippets` is [{field, keyword, snippet}] with each snippet being the keyword surrounded by 5 chars (CJK) or 5 words (ASCII) of context (`…` marks truncation), capped at 5 per block. The snippets often let you judge relevance without an extra mdp_read_block. Empty list → fall back to mdp_list_blocks or mdp_tree.

query.description: Single keyword or phrase to search for. Optional if `any_of` is provided.

any_of.description: Multi-keyword OR list. Each block is scored by total hit count across all terms. Each result row's `matched` field tells you which of these keywords actually hit that block. Use this when several candidate terms might apply — one call covers all of them.

function.name: mdp_list_blocks
function.description: Structural overview of a Markdown+ document — fallback entry point when the user's question has no identifiable keyword. If the question DOES name concrete topics or terms, prefer mdp_search_blocks first. Returns a metadata-only manifest [{id, type, status, title, line, keywords}], NOT body content. The `keywords` field is author-declared `keywords:` if present, otherwise the auto-extracted N-gram/PMI keyword list (plus structural tags like mermaid diagram type and table column headers).

depth.description: Nesting depth to include. 1 = top-level blocks only, 2 = include direct children, etc. Omit for all levels.

where.description: Filter by block attributes / metadata, e.g. {"type": "decision", "status": "open"}. Use the value "*" to match any present value of a key.

function.name: mdp_get_block_meta
function.description: Get one block's full metadata: id, type, line, depth, parent, children, title, summary, all author-declared key:value `metadata`, computed `auto_keywords` (dictionary-free N-gram + PMI + entropy + structural tags; empty when author already declared `keywords:`), and body line count. Still NO body content. Call after mdp_search_blocks / mdp_list_blocks to inspect a specific candidate before deciding to read it.

function.name: mdp_list_children
function.description: List the direct child block ids of a block. Use to walk a document's hierarchy one level at a time without pulling content.

function.name: mdp_read_block
function.description: Read a block's body markdown. This is the ONLY call that returns real content and spends tokens — call it last, only on the specific block(s) you actually need. The returned body includes the block's own header line, so it is a valid standalone Markdown+ snippet.

include_children.description: If true, return the whole subtree (child headers + bodies). Default false (own body only).

max_lines.description: Cap the number of returned lines. If hit, the response sets truncated:true.

function.name: mdp_resolve_xref
function.description: Resolve a block's relationships: parent, children, superseded-by / supersedes, and related ids. Each reference is resolved to a small descriptor (or marked found:false if it points nowhere). Use to follow decision history and cross-links.

function.name: mdp_tree
function.description: Return the full block hierarchy of a document as nested nodes ({id, type, status, title, line, children}). Metadata-only, no body content. Use for a one-shot structural overview of a whole document.
